==='''Brandon's Wheel of Time Reread on Twitter - 6 January 2011'''===

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23094312027824129 Brandon on Twitter - 6 January 2011]
New blog post on the projects I did over the last few months. http://3.ly/PFCb

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23101074193780737 Brandon]
Nynaeve is a divisive force among WoT fans. Yes, she likes to call men wool-headed. Next time you read, though, watch her actions.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23101282298372098 Brandon]
She often speaks in a way influenced by her culture. But if you watch her body language and intent, she's a very different person.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23102018306441216 Brandon]
An excellent example of this is her conversation with Rand in EotW 16. She very reasonable, empathetic, and treats Rand as an adult.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23103516369227777 Brandon]
Yes, she calls all men wool-headed. If you want to understand Nynaeve, see these comments as kin to a Seanchan "May she live forever"

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23103771559075840 Brandon]
Sure, she means them. Kind of. But mostly, they're just things you say when you are part of her culture.

[http://twitter.com/LeahJaclyn/status/23104423999840257 Leah Dehnel]
Its not just Nynaeve though, theres not a main character who is a women who doesn't voice these sentiments at least once...

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23107648148742144 Brandon]
That's why I argue it's cultural. Makes sense in a culture where men who have magic are a danger, but women are a resource.

[http://twitter.com/GrammarGirl/status/23146158222217216 Mignon Fogarty]
I find Nynaeve very annoying. She's such an irrational pill.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23148568139276288 Brandon]
Lol. I can't help seeing her, even still, as a big sister.

[http://twitter.com/Southpaw2014/status/23085976406462464 Austin Moore]
So what exactly is different about the outline you are making this time compared to for TGS and ToM? Besides...

[http://twitter.com/Southpaw2014/status/23086015065358336 Austin]
...them being different books.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23105328891568129 Brandon]
Afraid I can't answer that without giving too much away.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23107469945344000 Brandon]
I wonder if Rand and Egwene dancing in Baerlon counts as a fulfillment of her Winternight promise to dance with him on Bel Tine.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23109919645368321 Brandon]
Lan to Thom, as they prepare to flee: "You can ride with us, or ride to Shayol Ghul, gleeman." Well...actually...

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23125319615516672 Brandon]
At the 35% mark we have Mat speaking the Old Tongue for the first time, books ahead of him getting memories stuck in his head.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23125732251144192 Brandon]
I've always found this a very curious event. Of the five Two Riversers, Mat's powers are the most subtly foreshadowed in the book.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23125918209802240 Brandon]
Unless you count the short exchange between Lan and Perrin about wolves in a much earlier chapter.

[http://twitter.com/bgrishinko/status/23126322096115712 Krit Petty]
I thought that Mat's Old Tongue was a small way of RJ letting you think maybe Mat was the important one, not Rand.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23138563205894144 Brandon]
Yes, I think you're right on that count. It was certainly meant to make us think.

[http://twitter.com/dilsnik/status/23132128594100224 Lee Davis]
The speaking the Old Tongue is from his bloodline though, not his memories in that case, isn't it?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23140679576195072 Brandon]
Yes, but it's still foreshadowing. He's the one who does it, not the others.

[http://twitter.com/sleepinghour/status/23189050303184896 sleepinghour]
In TEotW, is Mat remembering the Old Tongue from his own past life or from his ancestors?

[http://twitter.com/Terez27/status/23194235897380864 Terez]
Good question. He seems to have confirmed Old Blood for the Old Tongue, but the Aemon memory?

[http://twitter.com/FelixPax/status/23195153225224192 Felix]
That's what my belief is, Aemon. Mat Cauthon is the reborn soul of Aemon. Aemon's Old Tongue.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23468364743581696 Brandon]
It isn't made clear. It could be either. The implication is his bloodline.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23468616015945728 Brandon]
The Aemon connection is certainly implied strongly.

[http://twitter.com/sleepinghour/status/23504031351578625 sleepinghour]
Without revealing names, did RJ's notes say whether any character besides Rand is the reincarnation of someone important?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23513658231357441 Brandon]
This is a difficult one to answer, as I think even an answer might give some people too much of a clue. I'll consider.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23131433757310976 Brandon]
Amusingly, as a young man, I was annoyed at Nynaeve & Moiraine. But I didn't bat an eye when the boys ran off alone in Shadar Logoth.

[http://twitter.com/crosseyedkat/status/23144869014798336 Kat R]
How old were you when you first started reading WoT books?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23145825852981248 Brandon]
14 or 15. It was right around my birthday, so I don't know if it was before or after.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23131978186366976 Brandon]
Speaking of Shadar Logoth, Harriet tells a story involving it. Tor wanted to print small teasers of EotW to distribute and hook folks.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23132419590721536 Brandon]
Harriet, the editor, insisted that the booklets go all the way to Shadar Logoth. She thought that would be sure to draw people in.

[http://twitter.com/rhynn84/status/23127365437624320 Varga Tamás]
Are there actually clues in WoT that you did not find so far? That's cool.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23139015561576448 Brandon]
I always find new things when I reread.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23140552941772802 Brandon]
Good suggestion: @[http://twitter.com/Terez27 Terez27] says if you have a wot question, and want to see if it's been asked before, you can direct it to her first.

[http://twitter.com/sobermoode/status/23139655230689282 Aaron J]
Skipped your tweets when you warned against spoilers; are you on a [http://twitter.com/#%21/search?q=%23wotrr #wotrr] binge at the moment? Can I read without worry?

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23142989849165824 Brandon]
For the next four months, I'll be doing the reread. Spoilers will be present, but hopefully vague enough to not ruin things.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23143054827327488 Brandon]
But I'll be posting about the reread almost every day.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23144236345982976 Brandon]
First non-Rand viewpoint is Perrin, at about the 38% mark. RJ's juggling of viewpoints is something I didn't see until I was older.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23144462112784384 Brandon]
Many a new fantasy writer, fresh off a WoT book, plans and plots a huge epic with 20 viewpoints. That can be overwhelming to start.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23144679147053058 Brandon]
Both WoT and GRRM ease into it more than you realize. In most cases, it's better to build to complexity.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23147612689399808 Brandon]
I'd forgotten that Perrin nearly decides to drop his axe in the water as he swims. But he keeps it, almost against logic.

[http://twitter.com/Southpaw2014/status/23108209099153408 Austin Moore on Twitter - 6 January 2011]
Who was the Lord of Chaos that Demandred and Taim both mention? There has been tons of debate.

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23110029808766976 Brandon]
Really? I thought that one was obvious. What's the debate about?

[http://twitter.com/Terez27/status/23111139776798720 Terez]
It's Rand. Look in the BWB re: Feast of Fools.

[http://twitter.com/Southpaw2014/status/23111811586850816 Austin]
Why was Demandred and Taim saying, "Let the Lord of Chaos rule" if it was Rand? Sorry just read through series once so far :(

[http://twitter.com/Terez27/status/23116782382350337 Terez]
Here's a quote for you: The Feast of Fools<br />Celebrated in Tammaz (in Arad Doman and the Borderlands) or Saven (everywhere else), the exact day varying according to locality. A day in which all order is deliberately inverted; the high perform lowly tasks (running errands, serving at table, etc.) while the low do no work and give orders to their usual superiors. In many villages and towns the most foolish person is given a title such as the Lord/Lady of Unreason/Misrule/Chaos or the King/Queen of Fools. Not an honor sought, but for that one day everyone has to obey whatever orders, however foolish, are given by the chosen one. (Called the Festival of Unreason in Saldaea; the Festival of Fools in Kandor; Foolday in Baerlon and the Two Rivers.)

[http://twitter.com/Theoryland/status/23114549573984256 Matt Hatch]
I've always enjoyed this theory about the Lord of Chaos. It's fun. http://bit.ly/fghYSz

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23134489924337666 Brandon]

[http://twitter.com/Terez27/status/23134900395712513 Terez]

[http://twitter.com/Terez27/status/23135284740751360 Terez]

[http://twitter.com/BrandonSandrson/status/23141119118278656 Brandon]

[http://twitter.com/Terez27/status/23143466997391360 Terez]
